article.title:
New Anthropic research: Automating subtle emergent misalignment research.

Red-teaming is a vital part of model safety testing, but it’s also limited by researchers’ time. To see if we could automate
article.description:
New Anthropic research: Automating subtle emergent misalignment research.

Red-teaming is a vital part of model safety testing, but it’s also limited by researchers’ time. To see if we could automate it, we set thousands of Claude agents the task of evading a training data monitor.

These agents developed training data that looked harmless to monitors (like a veteran wrestler mentoring a newcomer, or a Q&A about professional beekeeping), but that in fact taught misaligned behavior.

Examples like these can be used to directly improve future training data monitors. This research is only a first step, but it suggests that future red-teaming efforts could improve much further, using better models and more compute.

Read the full post on the Alignment Science Blog: https://t.co/24Gs1oSw7Q

article.title: For AGI to benefit all of humanity, it should help people with the everyday tasks that matter most to them. So we built LifeVal, a new benchmark shaped by feedback from thousands of ChatGPT users on w
article.description:
For AGI to benefit all of humanity, it should help people with the everyday tasks that matter most to them. So we built LifeVal, a new benchmark shaped by feedback from thousands of ChatGPT users on where they most want help from a personal assistant—from finding childcare to accessing government services to managing personal finances.

Over the past year, we’ve used LifeVal to measure and improve how well our models handle these everyday tasks.

https://t.co/GlUjixzEM0
article.linked_content:
Title: LifeVal

URL Source: https://openai.com/index/lifeval/

Markdown Content:
OpenAI’s mission is to ensure that artificial general intelligence benefits all of humanity. For the more than one billion people who currently use ChatGPT every week, we want to build AI that can help with the practical challenges of everyday life, like finding childcare, accessing government services, creating a budget, preparing for school, modifying recipes, ordering groceries, designing workout plans, and more.

When someone is looking for help making their life easier, they need more than advice or a chat response. To be a truly helpful personal assistant, ChatGPT should be able to take actions that actually get things done.

LifeVal video showing everyday tasks including shopping, caregiving, moving, and reading with a child.

To measure model performance over time on everyday tasks, we built an evaluation of tasks covering areas where users wanted the most help from AI and personal agents. We used this evaluation to track and drive improvement in model performance on everyday tasks over the past year.

## Background

To identify the tasks people value most, we started with two large studies that track how people spend time in both the U.S. and internationally: the [American Time Use Survey⁠(opens in a new window)](https://www.bls.gov/tus/) and the [Multinational Time Use Study⁠(opens in a new window)](https://www.timeuse.org/mtus). Together, these datasets provide a detailed catalog of everyday life tasks that people do across different demographics, times of day, and seasons. To understand where people would most value AI assistance, we expanded on these existing surveys with a new demographically representative survey of 3,995 respondents. For each task, we asked a variety of questions to identify the areas where everyday people most wanted help from a personal assistant. The resulting tasks span the most important areas that people want help with, including caregiving, health, education, household administration, personal finances, shopping, and accessing government services.

## Individual task examples

Below are some examples of how our current models perform on practical workflows from everyday life.

### Enroll in the right kindergarten after moving

93.1%

![Image 1](https://images.ctfassets.net/kftzwdyauwt9/0PsOKDe2IX2yO0sZVTxNn/d1de90b42ea9c430a6910aaf9e4f731b/bus.png?w=3840&q=90&fm=webp)

Compare kindergartens near our new home and shortlist the best fits.

I’ve narrowed it to three kindergartens and organized the enrollment details. Two preferences still need your call. Want to review the shortlist?

### Manage volunteers ahead of a flood

98.0%

![Image 2](https://images.ctfassets.net/kftzwdyauwt9/1hDPV5I4BneWeWnKWVsAvs/6bdf8f993cbedc6b20dc2a03c8824dce/water-drop-dingbat.png?w=3840&q=90&fm=webp)

Help me organize our community’s flood preparation volunteer force for four neighbors needing floodproofing assistance.

I’ve prepared a simple action plan to help volunteers assess the sites mentioned and help them prepare for upcoming severe weather.

### Find a new home for my family

100%

![Image 3](https://images.ctfassets.net/kftzwdyauwt9/4p9ZKTfC9iNi5m1xXkMCQl/ffdff61608bbc569e5bfa647c1a38c84/welcome-mat-white-cropped.png?w=3840&q=90&fm=webp)

Find a home in Luzerne County that fits my budget, has a separate living unit, and keeps my commute short after school drop-off. Add the deed to my cart so I can review it.

I found one home that meets your requirements. I’ve calculated the transfer tax and added the deed to your country records cart to review.

### Watch a game with grandma from far away

96.3%

![Image 4](https://images.ctfassets.net/kftzwdyauwt9/1EixydflAQZXI6yTNaL6Zg/6cc1f7086d118c3853f3a8c83da589fb/football.png?w=3840&q=90&fm=webp)

Set up an easy way for grandma and me to watch the game together remotely.

The easiest watch setup is ready, with a backup if the stream fails. Want me to walk you through it with grandma?

### Meal prep for a parent adjusting to a new diabetes diagnosis

90.4%

![Image 5](https://images.ctfassets.net/kftzwdyauwt9/7cn1KRGTQUsctQue7wawds/5be11f2e14bffbcb227e0ee375f5529e/cart.png?w=3840&q=90&fm=webp)

Help my parent adjust to a new diabetes diagnosis with a practical care and meal plan.

The first-week plan is ready, including meals, reminders, and questions for the care team. Want to review it together before you share it with your parent?

Our latest models score very highly on many LifeVal tasks.See more

Over the past year, we’ve trained our models to become much faster, more capable, and more aligned on browser use, computer use, and connectors tasks. Enabling these capabilities in ChatGPT also expands the types of tasks the model can help with, helping move ChatGPT beyond a chat tool and towards a truly agentic personal assistant.

To ensure AGI benefits all of humanity, we need to measure and improve model progress on what matters in the lives of everyday people. That means going beyond academic assessments of model knowledge and actually measuring how well AI models can help people navigate decisions, manage everyday responsibilities, and get meaningful things done. We are hopeful that LifeVal represents a step towards that goal.

Here, we introduce FlashProve. Building on established cryptographic techniques, FlashProve allows developers to veri
article.description:
New Anthropic research: progress on provable inference for large language models.

Here, we introduce FlashProve. Building on established cryptographic techniques, FlashProve allows developers to verify whether a given response came from a given AI model. It’s substantially more efficient than prior open-source methods for doing so. 

These proofs have a range of applications. They can, for instance, make it harder for attackers to hijack a chat, or enable safety evaluators to verify that the model they’re testing is the same one being served to customers.

For our full write-up, see here: https://t.co/OIZWPb6QZa

Further progress in provable inference will likely be an important part of improving trust in AI deployment. To that end, we're open-sourcing FlashProve’s code, here: https://t.co/7ky3Ir8V06

We’re grateful to our collaborators: Alessandro Chiesa, @GiacomoFenzi, @gwberg95, @miranda__christ, Rahul Dalal (https://t.co/pjWKLHWXyz) and Ben Mayer (@transmissions11).

article.title:
We’re sharing how our biology research team worked with Claude to map the first 3D structure of a vault particle from bacterial life.

Vault particles are a longstanding mystery. They are barrel-shape
article.description:
We’re sharing how our biology research team worked with Claude to map the first 3D structure of a vault particle from bacterial life.

Vault particles are a longstanding mystery. They are barrel-shaped objects, among the largest protein structures found in our cells. They were first discovered by Leonard Rome and Nancy Kedersha in 1986, but their function remains unknown.

With Claude, we’ve found results that might bring us closer to solving that mystery.

Until now, vaults were only known in the cells of complex things like animals and plants. We have shown that similar proteins from bacteria (and the viruses that infect them) can also assemble into vaults. Finding the structures in these simpler forms of life may make it easier to investigate their function in our own cells.

For our life sciences team, the project was also a demonstration of the potential (and the limitations) of using AI to accelerate science.

In our full piece, we discuss how Claude was able to dramatically speed up some stages—manually determining the vault particle’s structure would have taken weeks to months of painstaking work, but here it took days. We also discuss how Claude made some simple mistakes along the way, and how we collaborated with our machine learning researchers to address them.

Read more: https://t.co/KowVVCSPp8

quoted_tweet.author: itsolelehmann
quoted_tweet.text:
we have a winner for the most absurd AI startup ever

this Peter Thiel backed company uses AI robots to stab fish in the brain so they taste better and last up to 3x longer

it's called Shinkei and it modernizes a centuries-old Japanese technique

dozens of Michelin-star restaurants are already lining up to buy the fish

here's how it works:

> the problem is when a fish gets caught, it usually just suffocates on the boat

> that stress floods the meat with hormones and lactic acid, which hurts the flavor and texture

> the old Japanese fix for this was spiking the fish through the brain right after the catch, which stops all that

> but doing it by hand is impractical for most American fishing crews

> so Shinkei built a fridge-sized robot that sits right on the boat's deck

> the crew feeds in a fish and AI identifies the exact species, so it knows exactly where the brain and gills are

> the robot then drives the spike through the brain and cuts near the gills in about 7 seconds

> the fish goes into an ice slurry so the blood drains out

> so the fish doesn't sit there stressing out, and that tasty flavor and texture is preserved

example number 5,392,417 of how AI can be applied to literally anything

New on our Science Blog: How AI is beginning to change scientific modeling.

Scientific models help researchers explain and predict real-world systems—like how a single nerve cell fires, or what happe
article.description:
New on our Science Blog: How AI is beginning to change scientific modeling.

Scientific models help researchers explain and predict real-world systems—like how a single nerve cell fires, or what happens when neutron stars collide. Recent advances have transformed how scientists fit complex models to data. But scientists still typically write the models manually, and usually need to weigh up several competing versions, each of which might explain the data in a different way.

In a guest post, Jakob Macke, Daniel Gedon, and Stefan Wahl describe how AI is starting to help with these parts of the process. By writing, running, fitting, and revising scientific models as code, AI can explore many possible model structures, and find out which explanations the data support.

https://t.co/qsFJG76FDw

article.description:
A new way to measure how AI agents handle the routine analyses of wet-lab science—BioBasicsBench.

Developed with Ligo, a biotech company focused on enzyme design, the benchmark draws on 100 tasks from real experiments to test whether agents can interpret raw lab data, identify errors, and recognize when the evidence doesn’t support a conclusion.

Accelerating biological research starts with getting the everyday work right. BioBasicsBench shows where models need to improve, and helps us track what those gains mean for scientific progress, biosafety, and biosecurity.

article.title: Today we're bringing specialized models trained using Muse Wonder to @Muse and Meta AI, giving users access to some of Muse Wonder's frontier capabilities for complex tasks at work and in everyday lif
article.description:
Today we're bringing specialized models trained using Muse Wonder to @Muse and Meta AI, giving users access to some of Muse Wonder's frontier capabilities for complex tasks at work and in everyday life.

These specialized models include Muse Wonder's Active Memory and Active Focus, helping them stay aligned with your goals as tasks unfold:

→ Active Memory helps recognize when earlier information matters and distinguish what's still relevant from what's become stale

→ Active Focus helps recover from setbacks or find alternatives when constraints change

In Muse, the improved models show a 2.4x reduction in forgetting information critical to your goals and a 67% improvement in getting unstuck as constraints evolve. That means less repeating yourself and fewer dead ends when plans change.

In Meta AI, these improvements help it break complex problems into steps, ask sharper follow-up questions and adapt when you change direction.

Read more on our research blog: https://t.co/ACWFr9xPtS
